content.text: Episodes18Next episodeVideos18SummaryReviewers say 'Daredevil: Born Again' garners mixed reactions, applauding Charlie Cox and Vincent D'Onofrio's performances and mature storytelling. The darker themes and intense action sequences are praised, yet pacing issues and inconsistent tone are criticized. Some find the MCU integration and CGI distracting, while others appreciate new characters and cultural representation. The series is a noteworthy MCU addition, though it may not fully replicate the original's magic for all fans.AI-generated from the text of user reviewsFeatured reviewsGritty, character based, action packed. Marvel has takes you to the streets, and through the modern legal system!Daredevil is a comic that was given the "The Batman treatment" and a rebirth. Frank Miller who took the campy Adam West, Batman and rewrote the character into "The Dark Knight Returns" was given the same task in the 90s with Daredevil. That Daredevil has never been portrayed better than when Netflix launched Daredevil over a decade ago, and spun off 5 other series including "The Defenders". When all that was canceled I was so angry and upset about it, but Disney bringing back not just the old cast but old production crew in "Daredevil: Born Again" is nothing short of a miracle. This show so far has surpassed my expectations and of all Disney Plus content has become my most re-watched show. I am so excited for a second season and hope to see Charlie Cox's character show up in more Marvel projects besides She Hulk and Spiderman. Daredevil Born Again is great and I can't hype it up enough!!!A gritty but grounded return for "the man without fear".After years in limbo, Daredevil: Born Again marks a triumphant, if imperfect, return for Marvel's most grounded hero. The series reintroduces Matt Murdock (Charlie Cox) with a newfound maturity, exploring the cost of heroism and the fragility of redemption. From the first episode, it's clear that this isn't a simple reboot, it's a reawakening. Cox slips back into the role with quiet intensity, and Vincent D'Onofrio's Kingpin once again dominates every scene with magnetic menace. Their cat-and-mouse dynamic remains the show's beating heart.Visually, Born Again embraces its street-level grit. The fight choreography is brutal yet elegant, often relying on long takes and practical stunts that feel refreshingly authentic. The cinematography drenches Hell's Kitchen in moody reds and shadows, reinforcing the show's noir undertones.However, the season occasionally falters under its own ambition. The pacing drags in the middle stretch, with too much focus on subplots that lack emotional payoff. Some supporting characters, especially the new additions, feel underdeveloped, their arcs are more functional than memorable. And while the writing aims for emotional depth, a few dialogue-heavy scenes verge on melodrama.Still, when Born Again hits its stride, it soars. The moral tension, raw performances, and thematic weight elevate it beyond most superhero fare. It may not quite recapture the lightning of the Netflix original, but it stands tall as a thoughtful, mature continuation rather than a retread.A dark, mature return for DaredevilDaredevil: Born Again may be the most mature season of the entire series. Wilson Fisk's return as the so-called "savior" of New York and his rise to mayor raise the question of whether he has truly changed, or if this is simply another calculated performance aimed at total control of the city.This season delivers more than physical confrontations; it dives deep into the inner conflict of its protagonist. Daredevil is forced to question his motives, his limits, and the true cost of justice. The show's themes closely mirror real-world social and political tensions, giving the story added weight and relevance.From a production standpoint, Born Again looks outstanding. The music, cinematography, editing, and fight choreography are all top-tier. The finale ends on a strong cliffhanger, leaving audiences eager to see how Daredevil will confront the growing darkness hanging over the city.Great, but....Really enjoyed the new series. It's definitely back to it's original feel and quality. It's introduced some new characters and a new story.Sometimes it can be a bit OTT, but it's a comic book story, so I get that.Only negatives are that some of the fight scenes are a bit lazy and repetitive. The CGI of Daredevil running across rooftops is just plain terrible. To the point of being laughable.It's a good comebackDaredevil: Born Again feels like a strong return to Hell's Kitchen. It keeps the gritty tone I loved while pushing Matt Murdock into a more conflicted place emotionally. Charlie Cox still owns the role, and the show does a good job balancing brutal action with quieter, character-driven moments. It's not as tight or impactful as peak Netflix Daredevil, but it comes close enough to feel satisfying. Some pacing issues hold it back a bit, yet the heart, intensity, and moral struggle are still there. Overall, it's a solid continuation that respects the character and gives fans something worth sticking around for.More like thisRelated interestsDid you knowFAQ19DetailsContribute to this pageSuggest an edit or add missing contentEdit pageAdd episode
